scope_line: Scope: the n8n monorepo including source-available enterprise modules (*.ee), Instance AI, chat hub, MCP, task runners and CI. n8n Cloud operations and the external template gallery are out of scope.
limits: Repository evidence only, master at the tip named above. Enterprise modules (*.ee) are included; they need a licence to run. n8n Cloud operations, the template gallery and community-node certification processes are outside the repository. Single rater.
reading: **SAL 2**, joint highest in the sample. The AI workflow builder asks clarifying questions and produces a plan for approval before it builds (DEL-01 2, DEL-04 2), and Insights reports failure rates per workflow (LRN-03 2), so both core loops reach L2. **Blocks L3:** controls, not workflow: migrations have no enforced online strategy (ARC-02 2), entity export has no restore test or recovery objectives (ARC-09 2), definition rollback covers workflows only (GOV-05 2), and AI changes have no declared blast-radius limit (GOV-10 2).
confidence_note: Confidence for criteria whose reading did not change at the v0.7 migration was assigned at migration from the recorded evidence (high where it names the code path and its tests, medium where it names code but not every path, low where the reading is inferred or rests on documentation or absence); criteria re-read at migration were assigned from that re-reading.

persistent_data.evidence: Workflows, credentials, executions and data tables in the database.

schema_changes.evidence: TypeORM migrations (packages/@n8n/db/src/migrations) and data tables created at runtime.

multi_tenant.evidence: Re-read at the v0.7 migration under the tightened definition. Team projects have their own members and project roles (project admin, editor, viewer; packages/@n8n/permissions/src/roles/all-roles.ts) and members do not see other projects' workflows or credentials (packages/cli/test/integration/access-control/cross-project-access.test.ts:136-379). Team projects need a licence (quota:maxTeamProjects, packages/cli/src/license.ts:483-485); this assessment scores the licensed enterprise modules as shipped, as it does for workflow reviews and the AI builder. The v0.6 reading (false) treated projects as not isolated tenants.

hosted_service.evidence: Main, worker and webhook processes run as long-lived services, with multi-main and queue mode (packages/cli/src/scaling).

machine_actions.evidence: The public API and MCP server change workflows and credentials (packages/cli/src/modules/mcp).

agent_mutations.evidence: The AI workflow builder and Instance AI change workflows (packages/cli/src/modules/instance-ai, workflow-builder), and the agents builder writes agent configuration, skills and custom tools as drafts it can publish when the user asks (packages/cli/src/modules/agents/builder/agents-builder-tools.service.ts:397-405, 697-740).

evolution_auto_apply.evidence: AI-built changes pass approvals before they apply.

definition_change_path.evidence: Workflows, credentials, variables and data tables are definitions.

code_release_path.evidence: Re-read under the v0.7 rule for code inside definitions. The agents builder writes TypeScript custom tools that are stored on the agent and run in a V8 isolate (packages/cli/src/modules/agents/builder/agents-builder-tools.service.ts:1090-1123; runtime/agent-secure-runtime.ts), and the workflow builder may write Code-node scripts (packages/@n8n/ai-workflow-builder.ee/src/prompts/agents/discovery.prompt.ts:271-284). Both are sandboxed and versioned with the agent or workflow they belong to, so they are part of a definition and definition rollback (GOV-05) covers them. The earlier v0.7 reading (true) counted them as code releases.

ai_features.evidence: AI workflow builder, Instance AI and AI agent nodes (packages/@n8n/ai-workflow-builder.ee, packages/cli/src/modules/instance-ai).

ai_data_access.evidence: Instance AI reads workflows, executions and node parameters (packages/cli/src/modules/instance-ai).

ai_actions.evidence: Instance AI and the builder create and change workflows behind approvals.

change_kinds.name: Automations: workflows and their steps
change_kinds.evidence: Built and changed in the editor with no deploy; undo through workflow history restore and publishing an earlier version (packages/cli/src/workflows/workflow-history/workflow-history.controller.ts:22-91), with 24 hours of history kept without a licence and the current and published versions always kept (packages/@n8n/constants/src/index.ts:80, workflow-history-manager.ts:35-43). The AI workflow builder plans and drafts the workflow and a person publishes it (licensed feat:aiBuilder, packages/cli/src/controllers/ai.controller.ts:83; packages/@n8n/ai-workflow-builder.ee). Not 3: the draft carries no verification evidence and no policy (DEL-04 is 2).

change_kinds.name: AI agents: their instructions, tools, skills and knowledge
change_kinds.evidence: Agents module is on by default (packages/@n8n/backend-common/src/modules/module-registry.ts:80); agents are edited as drafts, published, and reverted to any earlier version (packages/cli/src/modules/agents/agent-publish.service.ts:124-176, 358-450). The agents builder drafts configuration and custom tools, tests the draft in preview chat, and publishes only when the user asks (builder/agents-builder-tools.service.ts:397-405, 567-569, 697-740). Not 3 for the same reason as workflows. Not main: a new surface beside workflows; its share of change requests is not evidenced.

change_kinds.name: Connections to other services (credentials)
change_kinds.evidence: Created and edited in the UI with no deploy (packages/cli/src/credentials/credentials.controller.ts:217, 264), but there is no history of earlier values and deletion is permanent (credentials.controller.ts:479); source control carries credential stubs without secrets. A path without undo is reach 0.

change_kinds.name: Add, update or remove community integrations
change_kinds.evidence: Installed, updated and uninstalled from the UI (packages/cli/src/modules/community-packages/community-packages.controller.ts:11-34), on by default (community-packages.config.ts:12-29). An integration with no published package needs an engineer to write a node (packages/@n8n/node-cli).

change_kinds.name: Instance settings and shared variables
change_kinds.evidence: Most instance settings are environment variables read at start (about 500 @Env settings in packages/@n8n/config/src/configs), so a change needs a restart or redeploy; variables are licensed (packages/cli/src/environments.ee/variables/variables.controller.ee.ts:30) and have no history; both roll back only through git source control.

change_kinds.name: Data tables used by workflows
change_kinds.evidence: Tables, columns and rows are created, changed and deleted in the UI (packages/cli/src/modules/data-table/data-table.controller.ts:104-412) with no history or restore. A path without undo is reach 0.

ai_delivery.evidence: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md at the root and in packages (cli, frontend, nodes-base), a Claude Code plugin (.claude/plugins/n8n), shared agent skills (.agents/skills), AI review rules (cubic.yaml, .agents/review-rules), an opencode harness pinned at harness-v0.3.0 from n8n-io/cat-bot (agent-harness.lock.json, scripts/agent-harness.mjs:17-31), and PRs from the n8n-cat-bot agent (.github/workflows/ci-owners-assign-reviewers.yml:31-37).
ai_delivery.note: AI-assisted engineering, not n8n evolving itself. It does not meet rule 12: the harness is pinned but its enforcement and limits live in another repository, nothing in this repository makes an agent's authority or merge a required check, and no GOV-10 limits on its changes were found. The instruction files and skills are documentation.

request.searched: The repository at the pinned commit: CHANGELOG.md (n8n's own releases, made by engineers), packages/cli/src/workflows/workflow-history, packages/cli/src/modules/insights, workflow-reviews.ee and instance-version-history. No operating records of real changes made through the product's request loop in a deployment are in the repository.

fix.searched: The same sources plus packages/cli/src/modules/breaking-changes and execution error records; no operating records of issues fixed through the product's loop in a deployment.

expansion.searched: The same sources; no records of capabilities launched and kept or killed through the product.

MAL-01.evidence: Data tables are created in the UI with typed columns; a DDL service creates real tables without deploy, with their own permissions and public API (packages/cli/src/modules/data-table: data-table-ddl.service.ts, data-table-permissions.ts; packages/cli/src/public-api/v1/handlers/data-tables). Scored at the lower reading under rule 11 because: Data tables are storage for workflows, not general business-object types with forms and relations.
MAL-01.alt_note: The September v0.3 pass scored 3 on the evidence above.

MAL-02.evidence: Data-table columns are typed (data-table-column.entity.ts); execution data has redaction policies (packages/cli/src/modules/redaction/redaction-policy.ts) but no field-level privacy classification.
MAL-02.alt_note: Redaction policies are a consumed privacy control, though not a field tag.

MAL-03.evidence: No declarable relations between data tables and no lifecycle states for user entities; workflow states are product-defined.

MAL-04.evidence: One generic rows API serves every data table (public-api/v1/handlers/data-tables); the rest of the API is hand-written per resource.
MAL-04.alt_note: Every defined entity type (data table) gets API presence without per-entity code.

MAL-05.evidence: Creating or altering a data table changes the rows API immediately, and each workflow exposed over MCP or webhooks changes the callable surface without a deploy.

MAL-06.evidence: Public API v1 with an OpenAPI description and structured validation errors (packages/cli/src/public-api/index.ts, public-api-validation-error.ts); no typed client generation or dry-run.
MAL-06.alt_note: Shared API types package (packages/@n8n/api-types) serves typed clients internally.

MAL-07.evidence: Workflow canvases and Form trigger pages are stored as data and can be tested before activation (packages/nodes-base/nodes/Form); application layout is code.
MAL-07.alt_note: Forms are admin-authored, validated and previewable layouts.

MAL-08.evidence: Generic grid for any data table and generic form rendering from field definitions; no configurable list and detail views for other objects.

MAL-09.evidence: UI strings externalised in an i18n package with community locales (33 locale files); no tenant theme editor or text overrides.

MAL-10.evidence: Workflows are machine-readable rules (triggers, If, Switch, Filter and 400+ action nodes) composed in the UI across all integrations and data tables; testable with pinned data and by debugging past executions; versioned in workflow history (packages/cli/src/workflows/workflow-history); authored by the AI workflow builder and Instance AI (packages/@n8n/ai-workflow-builder.ee, packages/@n8n/instance-ai). Scored at the lower reading under rule 11 because: If replaying a past execution does not count as simulation against history.
MAL-10.alt_note: The September v0.3 pass scored 4 on the evidence above.

MAL-11.evidence: Event bus with log-streaming destinations (webhook, syslog, Sentry) configured by admins (packages/cli/src/modules/log-streaming.ee, packages/workflow/src/message-event-bus.ts); webhook triggers; executions are logged and can be retried.

MAL-12.evidence: Code nodes run in separate task-runner processes with memory, payload, concurrency and time limits (packages/@n8n/config/src/configs/runners.config.ts:36-55) and module allowlists (packages/@n8n/task-runner/src/config/js-runner-config.ts:5-8), triggered by events and webhooks. No egress control found.
MAL-12.alt_note: Every clause except egress control is met.

GOV-01.evidence: Design-system components and axe-core scanning through a Playwright fixture (packages/testing/playwright/fixtures/a11y.ts) used by a few E2E tests.
GOV-01.alt_note: The scans run in PR E2E jobs, but cover only a few pages.

GOV-02.evidence: Audit events for users, workflows and credentials on the event bus, exported through log streaming; policy decisions are audited (packages/cli/src/modules/policy-infrastructure/policy-decision-audit.ts); workflow review activity is recorded (workflow-review-activity.service.ts); execution pruning sets retention. Scored at the lower reading under rule 11 because: Coverage across every entity and an in-product audit viewer were not verified.
GOV-02.alt_note: The September v0.3 pass scored 3 on the evidence above.

GOV-03.evidence: Redaction policies for execution data (packages/cli/src/modules/redaction) and execution pruning; no data-subject export or tag-driven erasure.

GOV-04.evidence: Scope-based permissions (packages/@n8n/permissions), admin type-availability policies enforced at save, publish, start and import (packages/cli/src/modules/type-availability-policies/README.md), and community package scanning (packages/@n8n/scan-community-package). Scanning does not gate every change: the pull-request security job runs only when files under .github/ change (.github/workflows/ci-pull-requests.yml:135, 496-502) and runs Poutine and Zizmor, which scan GitHub Actions workflows (sec-ci-reusable.yml:12-26); the container Trivy scan runs from the image build (docker-build-push.yml:757-790) with exit-code '0' (security-trivy-scan-callable.yml:51), so it reports but never fails. Corrected from 3 to 2 at the v0.7 migration, as the blind second and third ratings found.

GOV-05.evidence: Workflow history with versions and restore (packages/cli/src/workflows/workflow-history); other surfaces (credentials, variables, data tables, settings) roll back only through source control. The higher reading of 3 was dropped under the inventory rule (a 3 needs every default surface at 3): Credentials, variables, data tables and settings roll back only through source control.

GOV-06.evidence: Workflow review requests with an inbox, decision policy and a publish guard that blocks publishing until approved (packages/cli/src/modules/workflow-reviews.ee, workflow-review-publish-guard.service.ts:11-29); git-backed environments let changes be staged on another instance first (packages/cli/src/modules/source-control.ee).

GOV-07.evidence: Shared policy infrastructure runs registered @PolicyCheck classes at fixed points with cleared or blocked outcomes and audited decisions (packages/cli/src/modules/policy-infrastructure/README.md); review decision policy (workflow-review-decision-policy.ts).

GOV-08.evidence: Nodes are versioned so existing workflows keep their typeVersion; a breaking-changes module scans workflows and configuration against the target version with a rule registry and migration services (packages/cli/src/modules/breaking-changes/README.md); node engine compatibility checks (packages/@n8n/node-engine-compatibility). Scored at the lower reading under rule 11 because: If migrations are applied rather than proposed, or breaking changes lack a policy exception.
GOV-08.alt_note: The September v0.3 pass scored 4 on the evidence above.

ARC-01.evidence: Data tables are real database tables queried with SQL; a workflow index supports search (packages/cli/src/modules/workflow-index); no definition-driven index mapping.

ARC-05.evidence: Applies since multi_tenant was re-read as true. Projects share one instance and database; isolation is by project-scoped roles with cross-project access tests (packages/@n8n/permissions/src/roles/all-roles.ts, packages/cli/test/integration/access-control/cross-project-access.test.ts:136-379); licensed worker pools can route a project's executions to its own queue (packages/cli/src/scaling/pool-config.service.ee.ts:14-40, packages/cli/src/controllers/project-pool-settings.controller.ee.ts). No per-project quotas or noisy-neighbour detection, so not 3.

ARC-06.evidence: Performance E2E runs on pull requests (ci-pull-requests.yml:492, test-e2e-performance-reusable.yml) and nightly benchmarks (test-benchmark-nightly.yml, packages/@n8n/benchmark); per-surface limits not documented in the repository.
ARC-06.alt_note: A performance suite gates pull requests; only documented limits are missing.

DEL-02.evidence: Main, worker, webhook and task-runner processes ship as separate container images from one monorepo build (12 Dockerfiles).

DEL-03.evidence: pnpm workspace packages, a module system with explicit registration, and import restrictions in package lint configs (packages/cli/eslint.config.mjs); Playwright architecture enforced by janitor (packages/testing/janitor).
DEL-03.alt_note: Lint-enforced boundaries plus API types between packages.

DEL-05.evidence: Pull requests run unit, lint, E2E (including axe fixtures), database, smoke, frontend declaration, performance and security jobs with no draft filter (.github/workflows/ci-pull-requests.yml:280-508).

MAL-13.evidence: Declarative and programmatic custom nodes, community packages installed from the UI (packages/cli/src/modules/community-packages), frontend extension SDK (packages/@n8n/extension-sdk), workflow templates and agent tools. Scored at the lower reading under rule 11 because: Theme and text are not plugin points.
MAL-13.alt_note: The September v0.3 pass scored 3 on the evidence above.

MAL-14.evidence: User code runs in isolated task-runner processes with resource limits; community nodes are scanned and can be restricted by policy but run with full trust in the main process.
MAL-14.alt_note: Code-node isolation meets every clause except egress.

MAL-15.evidence: Node CLI with dev server and linting (packages/@n8n/node-cli, eslint-plugin-community-nodes), source-control branches, execution logs and pinned-data testing against a live instance.

MAL-19.evidence: Instance MCP server with scoped API keys, per-workflow tool availability and MCP evaluations (packages/cli/src/modules/mcp: mcp-scopes.ts, mcp-tool-availability.ts, evaluations).
MAL-19.alt_note: Each exposed workflow becomes a tool whose schema comes from its trigger definition.

ai.evidence: Instance MCP server with scoped keys (packages/cli/src/modules/mcp).

MAL-20.evidence: Instance AI gives a natural-language interface to workflows, executions, credentials and nodes, with plans and approval cards before execution (packages/@n8n/instance-ai/docs/architecture.md, tools.md:18-82); chat hub for members (packages/cli/src/modules/chat-hub); Instance AI evaluations run in CI (.github/workflows/ci-instance-ai-evals.yml).
MAL-20.alt_note: Instance AI aims to make workflows reachable without the UI and is evaluated in CI.

ai.evidence: Instance AI grounded in workflows and executions, with plans and approvals.

GOV-09.evidence: Scoped API keys and MCP scopes, approval cards for AI actions, policy checks and audit events; no idempotency keys or dry-run for API mutations.
GOV-09.alt_note: Manual test executions with pinned data act as a dry-run for workflows.

ai.evidence: Scoped keys and approval cards for AI actions; no idempotency or dry-run.

MAL-16.evidence: All connectors exchange a common item format and are joined by configurable mapping (expressions and field mapping in the UI), so a second system is mapping configuration (packages/workflow). Scored at the lower reading under rule 11 because: No canonical domain model, only a canonical transport format.
MAL-16.alt_note: The September v0.3 pass scored 3 on the evidence above.

MAL-17.evidence: Node SDK with credential types for auth, trigger and polling patterns and versioning (packages/@n8n/create-node, packages/@n8n/node-cli); admins install community connectors in the UI.
MAL-17.alt_note: Verified community nodes amount to certification.

MAL-18.evidence: Path-versioned public API (packages/cli/src/public-api/v1) with documented breaking changes (packages/cli/BREAKING-CHANGES.md); no deprecation windows.

EXP-01.evidence: Kernel of users and SSO, projects and roles, workflows, credentials, executions, data tables, chat and triggers from any channel; no business-domain nouns in core.
EXP-01.alt_note: Kernel primitives are not themselves configurable definitions, so 4 is a stretch.

EXP-02.evidence: New domains are expressible as workflows, credentials and data tables with no kernel change, but no domain shipped this way is evidenced inside the repository.
EXP-02.alt_note: The public template gallery (grade C) proves many domains.

EXP-03.evidence: Workflows export and import as JSON; source control pushes and pulls workflows, credential stubs, variables and tags between instances.
EXP-03.alt_note: A source-control branch is a versioned, installable bundle.

LRN-01.evidence: The insights module collects execution counts, failures and time saved continuously and shows them in the product (packages/cli/src/modules/insights); vendor telemetry with redaction (packages/@n8n/telemetry).

LRN-02.evidence: Evaluation test runs record metrics per workflow (packages/@n8n/db/src/entities/test-run.ee.ts) and insights record per-workflow outcomes; no triage workflow.
LRN-02.alt_note: Test runs are linked to the workflow they evaluate.

LRN-04.evidence: Insights cover executions only; nothing joins usage, support and delivery data.

LRN-06.evidence: The breaking-changes detection report recommends fixes before upgrades (packages/cli/src/modules/breaking-changes/detection-report.ts): evidence-backed recommendations for one area.

DEL-04.evidence: AI workflow builder and Instance AI turn requests into workflow changes behind approvals, per instance.
DEL-04.alt_note: The lane is broad and governed, not narrow and engineer-run.

ai.evidence: The builder and Instance AI change workflows behind approvals.

LRN-09.evidence: Evaluations run workflows over datasets and record metrics per test run (packages/cli/src/evaluation.ee, test-run.ee entity); agent evals rate agents (packages/cli/src/modules/agent-evals). Runs are not bound to a keep, revise or rollback decision.
LRN-09.alt_note: Test runs give a baseline and metric per workflow version.

LRN-10.evidence: The checks that gate the product's own AI-made changes are code that engineers change: builder graph and JSON validation (packages/@n8n/ai-workflow-builder.ee/src/code-builder/handlers/parse-validate-handler.ts:164-196, validation/programmatic.ts), policy checks registered as code (packages/cli/src/modules/policy-infrastructure/README.md), builder prompts (packages/@n8n/ai-workflow-builder.ee/src/prompts) and the AI evaluation suites in the repository (.github/workflows/ci-instance-ai-evals.yml, packages/@n8n/ai-workflow-builder.ee/evaluations). Operators keep their own evaluation datasets and evaluation workflows in the product (packages/cli/src/evaluation.ee) and agent evaluation datasets as data tables, behind a rollout flag (packages/cli/src/modules/agent-evals/agent-evals-flag-gate.ts); generated cases are drafted from the agent's configuration, not from failures (agent-eval-case-generation.service.ts:55-73). People improve these by hand; no failure or wrong pass is recorded against the check that missed it.
LRN-10.alt_note: Evaluation workflows are versioned in workflow history, and opt-in, licensed type-availability policies are admin-edited rules enforced at save and publish (packages/cli/src/modules/type-availability-policies/README.md:17-25); but evaluations do not gate publishing and policy rules are not versioned.

DEL-06.evidence: /healthz and /healthz/readiness (packages/cli/src/abstract-server.ts:139), Prometheus metrics (server.ts:172), instance version history (packages/cli/src/modules/instance-version-history) and settings APIs exposing configuration. Scored at the lower reading under rule 11 because: If the settings API is not a deployed-configuration snapshot.
DEL-06.alt_note: The September v0.3 pass scored 3 on the evidence above.

DEL-07.evidence: One preview codespace per pull request from the master prebuild (scripts/codespace-preview/preview.mjs), instance seeding scripts (scripts/instance-seeding), nightly benchmark infrastructure created and destroyed (test-benchmark-destroy-nightly.yml).

DEL-08.evidence: Playwright journeys (packages/testing/playwright/composables/journeys) with nightly coverage; no changed-path to journey map or adoption instrumentation at ship evidenced.
DEL-08.alt_note: Telemetry instruments features; janitor enforces test architecture.

LRN-07.evidence: The AI workflow builder and Instance AI change workflows when asked; nothing learns from runs without being asked.
LRN-07.alt_note: Insights capture experience that the AI can read on request.

ai.evidence: No AI involvement in this behaviour.

LRN-08.evidence: AI-built workflows pass automated graph and JSON validation while the builder works (packages/@n8n/ai-workflow-builder.ee/src/code-builder/handlers/parse-validate-handler.ts:164-196), and type-availability policies check them at save and publish where enabled; evaluations can compare a workflow version against a dataset before publishing (packages/cli/src/evaluation.ee), but they are run by people and are not tied to the publish decision. Re-read at the v0.7 migration under the tightened boundary (AI-built workflows and agents count as learned or AI-made changes); the reading stands at 2.
LRN-08.alt_note: If evaluations plus the review publish guard count as a pass or block decision.

ai.evidence: AI-built workflow versions can be evaluated against datasets before publishing, run by people (packages/cli/src/evaluation.ee).

ARC-02.evidence: TypeORM migrations with down steps for PostgreSQL and SQLite and a migration registry with tests (packages/@n8n/db/src/migrations); no enforced online strategy.

ARC-03.evidence: Multi-main setup with leader election and Redis locks, and queue mode with separate workers (packages/cli/src/scaling/multi-main-setup.ee.ts, leader-election-client.ts, redis-lock.service.ts), covered by tests.

ARC-04.evidence: Queue mode runs executions on Bull with Redis (packages/cli/src/scaling/scaling.service.ts:100-105); leader election keeps schedules on one main. Failed executions are kept and can be retried by hand.
ARC-04.alt_note: Run-once scheduling and visibility are in place.

ARC-07.evidence: Prometheus metrics endpoint (packages/cli/src/metrics/prometheus); no published objectives.

ARC-08.evidence: Code nodes run in separate task-runner processes (packages/@n8n/task-runner, task-runner-python); nodes have retry-on-fail and timeouts; community nodes run in-process.

ai.evidence: Retry-on-fail, timeouts and fallback models on agent nodes.

ARC-09.evidence: export:entities and import:entities move every database entity, optionally with data-table rows (packages/cli/src/commands/export/entities.ts); binary data and the encryption key are separate; no restore test or recovery objectives.

DEL-01.evidence: The AI workflow builder plans before building: it asks typed clarifying questions and produces a plan with a trigger, steps, suggested nodes and specifications that the user approves (packages/@n8n/ai-workflow-builder.ee/src/types/planning.ts, agents/planner.agent.ts). The plan has no acceptance criteria or risk class.
DEL-01.alt_note: A confirmed, structured plan with clarifying questions approaches levels 3 and 4.

ai.evidence: The planner asks clarifying questions and drafts a plan (ai-workflow-builder.ee/src/types/planning.ts).

DEL-09.evidence: Workflow versions are published deliberately, and frontend features are gated per instance; there are no cohort rollouts for workflow changes.

DEL-10.evidence: Workflows can be deactivated at runtime; there is no global kill switch for AI-made changes.

LRN-03.evidence: Insights report failures and failure rates per workflow (packages/cli/src/modules/insights/insights.service.ts:181-268) and error workflows fire on failures.
LRN-03.alt_note: Failure rates per workflow approach friction detection.

LRN-05.evidence: Failed executions keep the failing node, input and error; the AI assistant can explain a node error on request.
LRN-05.alt_note: On-request AI debugging with node context approaches level 3.

ai.evidence: The AI assistant explains node errors with context on request.

GOV-11.evidence: Instance AI wraps resolved node parameters and external responses as untrusted data (packages/cli/src/modules/instance-ai/extract-resolved-node-parameters.ts:378-382); changes do not record their source inputs.
GOV-11.alt_note: Untrusted data is separated systematically in Instance AI.

ai.evidence: Instance AI wraps external data as untrusted (extract-resolved-node-parameters.ts:378-382).

ai.evidence: No AI involvement in this behaviour.

AIR-04.evidence: Instance AI looks up workflows within the user's scopes (instance-ai.adapter.service.ts) with folder-scope tests (__tests__/instance-ai-folder-scope.test.ts, instance-ai-folder-scoped-listing.integration.test.ts).

AIR-05.evidence: Evaluation harness with evaluators, datasets and LangSmith runs for the workflow builder and Instance AI (packages/@n8n/ai-workflow-builder.ee/evaluations).

AIR-06.evidence: Instance AI evals run automatically on pull requests touching AI paths (.github/workflows/ci-instance-ai-evals.yml:18-21) and builder evals on minor releases (test-evals-ai-release.yml); no blocking threshold was found.
